checks.Title: Re-enter through change, not summary
checks.Evidence: The opening establishes the present situation cleanly (the forty free minutes, the heist logistics), but the piece almost immediately pivots into extensive backward-looking recap: 'After Tidewell it started including names... After Crimson the count had stopped running backward,' and later entire paragraphs are spent reconstructing the prior operation's outcome ('The Protocol was dissolved... the endowment funded... Priya in the cooperative's safe house') via direct narrated summary rather than through scene-level inference.
checks.Fix: Cut the explicit 'After Tidewell... After Crimson' exposition and the summarized aftermath recap, and instead let the changed present—Vox's four-channel setup, the eased rapport with Rook, Boiler's community-center project—carry the history implicitly through action and dialogue rather than through stated backstory.

checks.Title: Reintroduce names like an old friend would
checks.Evidence: Some returning characters get vivid reactivation tags—Vox's healed forearm graze and her narrowing 'four channels' philosophy, Ekow's notebook-touch tic—but others like Lace, Boiler, and Scout are reintroduced mostly through job-function labels ('Lace inside,' 'Boiler on the freight lane') before any embodied gesture accrues, and Rook herself gets no reactivating tag at all despite being the POV anchor a returning reader would want re-grounded in.
checks.Fix: Give each major returning character (especially Lace and Boiler) one small physical or behavioral beat at first mention in this node—before their utility to the job is explained—so old readers recognize them as people, not slots.

checks.Title: Refresh proprietary terms on a lighter touch than the gateway
checks.Evidence: Proprietary terms like 'Crimson,' 'Tidewell,' 'Helix facilities,' 'Phase 0/Phase 1,' 'the Protocol,' 'the Stems,' and 'Old Harbor' are dropped in with zero re-glossing context — e.g., 'After Crimson the count had stopped running backward' and 'the other two Helix facilities still out there, still someone else's problem' assume the reader already carries full definitions rather than re-teaching them through context.
checks.Fix: Fold a brief contextual cue into first uses of key proprietary terms per node (e.g., 'After Crimson — the job that had cost her the two names she still wouldn't say aloud — the count had stopped running backward') so returning readers are gently reminded and newcomers aren't left guessing.

checks.Title: Never an acronym before its term
checks.Evidence: NGRA appears in Ekow's introduction ('Ekow Ato. Former NGRA. Twelve years independent operations...') with no full-term expansion anywhere before or after; similarly GLMZ recurs repeatedly ('all GLMZ work', 'GLMZ afternoons') without ever being spelled out on the page.
checks.Fix: Insert the full term in-voice at first use, e.g. 'Former NGRA — National Guard Reserve Auxiliary, or whatever cover the acronym still carried' and similarly gloss GLMZ ('the Great Lakes Metro Zone, GLMZ to anyone who'd lived here') before its first bare use.

checks.Title: Pay the previous book its due, then move
checks.Evidence: The node opens directly into a new job (the Rook heist/art recovery, then a sprawling continuation into the Protocol/Lotus arc) without any early beat that names what the previous book's ending cost or won; the only acknowledgments of past events ('After Tidewell,' 'After Crimson') are folded in as internal characterization deep in the middle of a new operation rather than as an opening beat confirming the prior victory's weight before turning forward.
checks.Fix: Open with a short, contained beat—before the new job's mechanics take over—that explicitly shows the tangible, lasting effect of the previous book's climax (e.g., a concrete change in Rook's world or relationships that only exists because of how the last book ended), then transition into the Headcount job.

checks.Title: Open the door the last ending left ajar
checks.Evidence: The node never names a specific thread from a prior book's ending — the closest analogue is the recurring 'count' motif and vague references to 'Tidewell' and 'Crimson,' but these are treated as backstory texture, not an open question the reader was left holding. The story instead opens a brand-new job (the Headcount sculpture) and lets it balloon into an entirely new, self-contained arc (the Protocol/endowment/Lotus dissolution) with no stated connective tissue to what a returning reader was promised at the last book's close.
checks.Fix: Open by explicitly naming the unresolved question the previous book ended on (e.g., what the 'count' running forward actually obligates her to, or an unfinished consequence of Crimson) and show the Headcount job snagging on that exact thread before it grows into the larger Lotus conspiracy.

checks.Title: Reward the long memory without taxing the short one
checks.Evidence: Extensive callback machinery (Casimir's list/Berhane Haile reveal, Vox's four-channel arc, the diner-counting motif, Scout's dual-presence card) is transparently built for returning readers, but several passages assume prior-book context without re-grounding it in-scene — e.g., 'After Tidewell it started including names' and 'After Crimson the count had stopped running backward' are dropped as bare proper nouns with no immediate explanation of what Tidewell or Crimson were, forcing a first-time reader to infer meaning entirely from context rather than being given a self-sufficient gloss.
checks.Fix: Add a brief in-scene appositive or sensory anchor each time Tidewell and Crimson are invoked (e.g., 'After Tidewell — the job that had gone wrong in a way she still counted differently — the names started') so newcomers get a functional foothold while returning readers still get the deeper resonance.

checks.Title: Escalate, don't repeat
checks.Evidence: The node explicitly frames itself against the prior arcs ('The first time she'd counted exact change. The second, who came through. The third, names. This time the count had no number.') and the stakes do widen from a heist to institutional dissolution, but the middle stretch reprises the exact heist-assembly beats (crew calls to Lace/Vox/Scout/Boiler, building recon, camera counting, permit-pulling) almost procedurally identical to prior-book structure before the escalation into the Protocol plot kicks in.
checks.Fix: Compress or transform the familiar crew-assembly/heist-recon sequence (which reads as a structural repeat of prior installments) so the escalation into institutional-scale stakes begins earlier and the 'new' texture (unresolved forward-count, Boiler's civic pivot, Ekow's confession) gets more page-time relative to the repeated procedural setup.
